feature: Cutting part of a shape says what it cannot do
summary: Draw a marquee over half a rectangle or a piece of text and press Command X and the shape stays where it is, with one line at the bottom of the canvas saying a piece can only be taken out of a picture and that clearing the marquee cuts the whole layer. Backspace over the same marquee says the same thing instead of doing nothing at all.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. "Say when a piece cannot be cut out" is on by default; "Copy takes the layer you picked" must also be on, which it is by default.

try.do: Open a new document and draw a rectangle with R.
Press V and click the rectangle to pick it.
Press M and drag a marquee over the left half of it.
Press Backspace over the same marquee.
Press Escape to clear the marquee, then Command X again.
Undo, then paste a screenshot in, pick it, marquee its corner and press Command X.

evaluate: Does the line at the bottom land where your eye already is, or did you miss it and think the key did nothing?
Is refusing the right answer, or would you rather Photonz turned the shape into a picture and cut the piece out for you?
Does "Clear the marquee to cut the whole layer" tell you enough, or should it name the key that clears it?
Is "Only a picture can have a piece taken out" true enough to your ears, given a rectangle looks like a picture on screen?
Does the line stay up long enough to read without hanging around?
rough: Option Backspace, which fills the marquee, still does nothing and says nothing over a shape. I left it alone because this task was about cut and delete, and a fill that does not happen destroys nothing, but the family now disagrees with itself. Filed as its own task.
The way out is described ("Clear the marquee") but the key is not named. Escape does it. Naming it would make the line longer and the pill wider, so I left it as a judgment for you.

A picture that has been cropped or turned gets its own wording ("This picture is cropped or turned") and I could not reach that case in the walk, so it is covered by tests rather than by a screenshot.

The task offered turning the shape into pixels as the other answer. That is a real feature with its own decisions (it is destructive, the shape stops being editable, it needs a menu item and a name), so it is filed separately rather than smuggled in behind Command X.
Screen Recording was granted, so both screenshots here are real window captures, not offscreen renders.
